newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cements, millers keep Egyptian shares up.
newsitem.headline: Cements, millers keep Egyptian shares up.

text.p: Cements and millers pulled up Egyptian share prices on Wednesday but most shares in the banking sector slipped in relatively thin trade.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose 0.90 points to close at 381.96 from 381.06 on Tuesday in about average turnover of 46.8 million pounds ($13.8 million).
Brokers said the market would probably stay within a narrow range until newly launched mutual funds start buying or the government offers more privatisation stock for sale.
"We still expect the market to move sideways in the short term, although there is capital waiting to be invested," said international securities house ING Barings.
The two most active stocks of the day were Amriyah Cement and Egyptian Tora Portland Cement. Both were gainers, Amriyah by 0.50 to close at 84.50 pounds and Tora by 0.44 to 97.50, the CMA said.
Helwan Portland Cement rose more steeply in lower volume, ending the day 1.20 up at 78.00 pounds.

The millers, often the barometers of sentiment on the Egyptian market, gained across the board, despite a report in the government press that the state would not relinquish majority control of those it continues to dominate.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills, one of three in which the state now holds less than 50 percent, was most active. It ended 2.3 percent higher at 92.25 pounds.
Sentiment in banks was negative with few exceptions and Commercial International Bank (CIB) led the way down, losing 4.28 to 81.50 in trade worth 3.4 million.
Misr International Bank/MIBank also fell, despite preparations for a GDR issue. The stock closed at 755.00 pounds, 5.00 pounds lower.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 595.56 from 598.87 points on Tuesday. The index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 262.93 from 261.03 points.
Out of the 85 shares traded on Tuesday, 33 gained, 20 lost and 32 ended unchanged.
